events.argument: {"text":"The experience was clear and fairly easy. I liked having distinct archival, comparison, and teaching goals rather than treating every combination as stronger evidence. Board five made collecting disagreement useful, and the final board gave me a reason to reuse a faithful selection for a later compared lesson. I would keep those multi-purpose boards and the exact proof visibility. I would shorten the repeated laws and omit unused roots from the default view; the large JSON responses outweighed the actual decisions. The first two boards work as a quick introduction but did not need exploration. I stopped because all six boards and their public goals were complete."}

Board five made collecting disagreement useful, and the final board gave me a reason to reuse a faithful selection for a later compared lesson. I would keep those multi-purpose boards and the exact proof visibility. I would shorten the repeated laws and omit unused roots from the default view; the large JSON responses outweighed the actual decisions. The first two boards work as a quick introduction but did not need exploration. I stopped because all six boards and their public goals were complete.

laws.permanent: Inputs remain indefinitely. No inventory, resource budget, score or action minimum. Equivalent meaning AND proof alternatives reuse an existing idea. Copies may have different labels but the same evidence.
laws.goals: Each goal needs one exact-scope account. independent means at least one proof per claim with two or more distinct roots referring to the SAME subject. faithful means at least one singleton proof per claim from the named origin. any accepts a nonempty proof. Different goals may use different accounts; contradictory accounts can coexist.
laws.honesty: All records, root identities, recipes, exact previews and goals are public. These are invented rules, not laws of historical progress or a model that decides scholarly truth.
